deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It holds two unrelated memoranda.

(A) Top, headed 1842: a continuation of the book-acquisition / reading list from fol. 80, which is headed 1841. The entries are:
- 'Der Frauen Tagebuch' by Henriette Hanke, January 1842.
- 'Victorine, ein Roman' by Henriette von Bissing, January 1842, 2 volumes.
- Henriette Hanke, sämmtliche Schriften, vols. 13-16, 17-20(?), 22-28. This continues the 'sämmtl. Schriften 1-4=12' entry on fol. 80.
- Hamann's Schriften, Theil 8.

(B) Below, headed 1850-1851: a ranked list of Göttingen professors with sums of money. Among them are Gauss, Wöhler, Weber, Listing, Ewald, Langenbeck, Waitz, Mitscherlich, Hausmann, Sartorius and Lücke.
- The amounts are in the Hanoverian notation Thaler.gute Groschen.Pfennig. One Thaler is 24 gGr and one gGr is 12 Pf. Consistent with this, no groschen figure exceeds 23 (e.g. Reibstein 59.23.8) and no pfennig figure exceeds 11.
- The main block (Haveman 281 down to Listing 21.0.0) is sorted in strictly decreasing order. Gauss himself stands at 150 Thlr 21 gGr. A second block below the rule (Linsing ... Gerke) lists further persons.
- The facing page (fol. 82) has the analogous list for 1849-1850, e.g. Gauss 148.11.
- Fol. 82 also shows how individual figures arise: a salary multiplied by a percentage rate. For example, 'Ewald 1200 à 1½' gives 18 Thlr, and 'Wagner 1800 à 1¾' gives 31.12, i.e. 31½ Thlr.
- This suggests the figures are assessed charges proportional to income (an income-tax or levy assessment), or possibly distributions such as fee/contribution shares. These are most plausibly connected with Gauss's administrative work on Göttingen university finances and the professors' widows' fund around 1845-1851. That identification is my inference, not stated on the page.

The only 'computation' is implicit: unit conversion and sorting. There is no derivation to reconstruct.
errors: The second (lower right) block is not monotone: Reibstein 59.23.8 is listed above Frick(?) 64.7.4, unlike the strictly decreasing main list. This may be deliberate (a different category) or a slip in ordering; it is not a mathematical error.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely bibliographic and administrative: a reading list and a table of monetary sums for colleagues. It contains no mathematical content. Its only interest is biographical or institutional, documenting Gauss's involvement with university financial records around 1850.

checkable.asserts: Wagner 1800 Thlr at 1 3/4 percent gives 31 1/2 Thlr = 31 Thlr 12 gGr (fol. 82 entry '31.12'), confirming the 24-groschen Thaler.
Ewald 1200 Thlr at 1 1/2 percent gives 18 Thlr (fol. 82).
Gauss 150.21 exceeds Baum 150.10 in pfennig (1 Thlr = 288 Pf, 1 gGr = 12 Pf), consistent with the ordering.
Reibstein 59.23.8 is smaller than Frick 64.7.4, so the lower block is not in decreasing order.
Gauss's amount rose from 148.11.0 (1849-50) to 150.21.0 (1850-51), a difference of 2 Thlr 10 gGr = 696 Pf.

transcription_corrections: Lines 1 and 3: 'Gräf.[?] Hahn[?]' should read 'Henr. Hanke', i.e. Henriette Hanke, the Hannover novelist. The first title is 'Der Frauen Tagebuch von Henr. Hanke. Januar 1842'. The 'Henriette Heyke[?]' on fol. 80 is likewise Henriette Hanke.
The Hanke volumes read '13-16, 17-20(?), 22-28'; the middle number is blotted and may be 20 or 21.
'Frick[?]' could also be read 'Fück'/'Frück'; the reading is uncertain.
'Haveman 281' is written 'Haveman̄' (double n by macron), i.e. Havemann.
'Lücke 136.12.1' is correct; 'Thöl 71:0' is written with a colon.
